clue.text: Like a slim and wiry bare bum

indicators.note: bum is used as an adjective meaning bad or faulty, so the letters come out wrong and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something bared has its covering stripped, so the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters stripped away

explanation.surface: A rude description of someone's skinny, sinewy bare backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'bare' and 'bum' look like they belong to the body being described, but one strips 'wiry' and the other shuffles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Similar and like are synonyms, both meaning resembling something else.

clue.text: Tanner's belt put underneath newspaper

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to lamp someone is slang for hitting them, to belt them

explanation.surface: A leather tanner's belt is placed beneath a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'put underneath' places the second piece below the first. 'Tanner' suggests a leatherworker, but it means something that gives you a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunlamp emits ultraviolet light to give a person a suntan, so it is a tanner.

clue.text: One who sets puzzles beginning to reconsider the object's value

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter only
it is the pronoun for an object

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter starts to rethink what an item is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who sets puzzles' is the setter, who in crosswords is me.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, so it can mean value.

clue.text: Lion with tummy trouble pursued by idiot husband in Tarzan outfit

indicators.note: an upset stomach churns things about, so the big cat's letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a clot is a fool
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A jungle scene: a sick lion is chased by a foolish husband dressed as Tarzan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursued by' puts the idiot and husband after the shuffled lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan is famously pictured wearing only a loincloth, a strip of cloth round the hips.

clue.text: Chekhov, for instance, starts to rewrite unpublished short stories including Ariadne and Neighbours

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, taken one from each

parts.words: rewrite unpublished short stories including Ariadne and Neighbours
parts.note: the first letter of each of the seven words

explanation.walkthrough: Ariadne and Neighbours really are Chekhov short stories, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov was a writer from Russia, so he is an example of a person of that nationality.

clue.text: Mistake seen in second-rate Turner?

parts.note: B is the second grade, as in a B-movie
something that loops goes round and round, a whimsical kind of turner

explanation.surface: An art critic spots an error in a lesser painting by J.M.W. Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter; the question mark flags a made-up word for anything that turns in loops.
explanation.definitionFit: A blooper is an informal word for an embarrassing error, especially one caught on film.

clue.text: Diminutive miner's boron powder left around flue, oddly

parts.note: B is the chemical symbol for boron
ash is the powdery residue of burning

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered positions, first and third

parts.note: the first and third letters of the word
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A short miner's chemistry: boron powder left round a chimney flue.
explanation.walkthrough: Bashful is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White, who work in a mine. 'Left around' is loose: L ends up after the two letters rather than surrounding them.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White are small miners, and one of them is named Bashful.

clue.text: Work with jerk that's full of spirit

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A lively, high-spirited person works alongside a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of spirit' sounds like lively, but it means filled with liquor. An optic is the measuring device fitted to an upturned bottle in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub optic is a measure attached to an inverted bottle of gin, whisky and so on, so it is literally filled with alcohol.

clue.text: Spirited fighting over hospital's lab equipment

indicators.note: things fighting are thrown about in a scrap, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the shuffled word above the hospital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Petri dish is a shallow glass or plastic dish used in laboratories for growing bacterial cultures.

clue.text: Date with whipped cream on

indicators.note: whipped cream is beaten and churned, so these letters are beaten into another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A dessert of dates served topped with whipped cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' suggests the fruit, as the cream encourages; here it is a romantic outing or affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, and to date someone is to have one, so the noun date and romance overlap.

clue.text: One who bloomed following a period of self-reflection

definitions.text: One who bloomed following a period of self-reflection

parts.words: One who bloomed following a period of self-reflection
parts.note: surface reading: a person who flourished after some time spent thinking about themselves

parts.words: One who bloomed following a period of self-reflection
parts.note: setter's reading: the Greek youth who gazed at his own image in a pool and was turned into a flower

explanation.surface: Someone blossomed personally after a spell of introspection.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the youth fell in love with his reflection in water, pined away, and became the flower that bears his name; 'self-reflection' is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical youth was transformed into a spring flower, so he literally bloomed after staring at his own image.

clue.text: Add dash symbol

parts.note: to tot up is to add up a sum
an em is a long dash in printing

explanation.surface: An instruction to insert a punctuation mark into a piece of text.
explanation.walkthrough: An em dash is the long printer's dash, named for the width of the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or creature serving as the emblem of a clan, so it is a symbol.

clue.text: Old Greek building's highest floor?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: relating to ancient Athens and its region
second meaning: the room at the top of a house under the roof

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the top storey of a Greek temple; the two halves are separate senses. The question mark admits that a roof space is only loosely a floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Attica was the region around Athens, giving the adjective for its dialect, and the same word names a room in the roof space.

clue.text: Covid-19? In a manner of speaking, there isn't any left

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for the side opposite right is absent, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: inflection is the rise and fall in the voice, a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A wry remark that, so to speak, no Covid remains anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway phrase, but it is the source word; L for left is then removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Covid-19 is a viral illness passed between people, an example of a contagious disease; the question mark marks it as an instance.

clue.text: You, say, or I, say, abandoning the Church of England

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the letters for the established church drop out

parts.note: to pronounce is to say or articulate
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone renounces the Church of England, perhaps with a declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'say' tricks the eye: the first marks examples, the second is the verb that loses its church.
explanation.definitionFit: You and I are personal pronouns, words standing in place of a noun naming a person.

clue.text: Acutely aware of concerning article written by degree students

parts.note: on means about or concerning
the definite article
BA is the Bachelor of Arts degree
L stands for a learner, so two of them make students

explanation.surface: Someone keenly aware of an essay written by university students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written by' places the degree and students after the article; L for learner comes from British L-plates on learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball is an idiom for being alert and quick to understand.

clue.text: Toilet queue overwhelms a gutless turnstile-operator

parts.note: a line is a queue of people
taken as written

indicators.note: with its guts removed, the hyphenated word keeps only its outermost letters

parts.note: just the first and last letters of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A crowd waiting for the loos pushes past a skinny attendant at the gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a basic toilet, typically in a camp or barracks.

clue.text: Club secretaries essentially switch sides at the start of meal

indicators.text: switch sides at the start of

the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the eleven

explanation.walkthrough: The opening L (left) of the meal is switched to R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short heavy stick carried by police, a kind of club.

clue.text: During chat, the other half of cake is put in sauce

the second pair of letters of the four-letter word, replacing the first pair

explanation.definitionFit: Ketchup is a tomato-based condiment, a familiar sauce.

clue.text: Making amorous advances, former US politician overlooks old queen

parts.note: Henry Kissinger was US Secretary of State in the 1970s
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

clue.text: Where a fire is prematurely extinguished in the middle of ancient structure

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of wood for burning
amid means among or in the middle of

explanation.surface: A fire goes out too soon in the heart of some old ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian pyramids are monumental tombs built thousands of years ago.

clue.text: Edit photo of exotic bird, erasing an expression that conveys urgency

taken as written, the letters removed

clue.text: Beat time on drum, topless, causing hysterics

taken as written, before losing its first letter

clue.text: Spin around book and say 'don't judge it by its cover'

clue.text: On board, I impress drunk mates with golf club

clue.text: Loiter about among low rugby goal posts

clue.text: Wheels, what they do, and what they carry?

clue.text: One minute ahead, Charlie ushers in a black taxi

taken as written
